instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: The ones who consider are named in the accounts of faith and of a decision: Sarah who counts the promiser faithful in Heb 11:11, God counted able in Heb 11:19, the reproach of Christ in Heb 11:26, Sarah's womb in Rom 4:19, and in Mat 1:20 Joseph, son of David, considering while an angel of the Lord comes.
observations.grounds: since she considered him faithful who had promised

observations.text: People are named as those regarded or counted as something: Nabal in 1Sa 25:25, a brother in 2Th 3:15 and 1Pe 5:12, servants of Christ in 1Cor 4:1, Christ known by the flesh in 2Cor 5:16, masters in 1Ti 6:1, rulers named by Jesus in Mar 10:42, the potter in Isa 29:16 and Lam 4:2, man in Isa 33:8, the men in Exo 5:9, the treasurers in Neh 13:13, and Solomon whose silver counts for nothing in 1Ki 10:21 and 2Ch 9:20.
observations.grounds: a faithful brother as I regard him

observations.text: Where the word is a weight, a link or regard for a king, the persons named are the doers around it: the man with the ring in Gen 24:22, the priests before whom the gifts are weighed in Ezr 8:29, the son of man in Eze 5:1, Samson in Judg 15:3, man and God in Ecc 3:18, Elisha, the Lord and Jehoshaphat in 2Ki 3:14, the priests in 2Ch 5:11.
observations.grounds: As the Lord of hosts lives

observations.text: The regard runs from God to people in Gen 4:5, Job 35:13, Job 37:24, Psa 144:3, Jer 24:5 and Lam 4:16: given to man and to the exiles, withheld from Cain, the empty cry, the wise in their own conceit, and a scattered people.
observations.grounds: what is man that you regard him

observations.text: The regard is asked from people to God in Deu 9:27, 2Ch 6:19 and Psa 80:14: they ask him to regard the prayer and the vine, and not to regard the stubbornness of the people.
observations.grounds: Turn again, O God of hosts

observations.text: In Psa 28:5 and Isa 5:12 the regard that should run from people to God's works is refused: they do not regard his deeds.
observations.grounds: they do not regard the works of the Lord

observations.text: In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 the question runs from the Lord to the one he speaks to, about Job: the considering asked for is directed at a third person.
observations.grounds: Have you considered my servant Job

observations.text: Where a person or thing is counted as something, the regard runs from one person to another, or to a thing: a brother not counted an enemy in 2Th 3:15, masters counted worthy in 1Ti 6:1, the potter not counted as clay in Isa 29:16, silver counted as nothing in 1Ki 10:21, and the others of 1Sa 25:25, 1Pe 5:12, 1Cor 4:1, 2Cor 5:16, Mar 10:42, Lam 4:2, Isa 33:8, Exo 5:9, Neh 13:13 and 2Ch 9:20.
observations.grounds: Do not regard him as an enemy

observations.text: In Heb 11:11, Heb 11:19, Heb 11:26, Rom 4:19 and Mat 1:20 the considering runs from the one who believes toward God's promise and power, toward the reproach of Christ, toward one's own body, or toward a decision to be taken.
observations.grounds: He considered that God was able

observations.text: Where the word is a weight or a link, no direction of a mind is stated: the weight of a ring, gifts weighed, the balances, in regard to the Philistines or the children of man; in 2Ki 3:14 the regard runs from Elisha to the king.
observations.grounds: I have regard for Jehoshaphat

observations.text: In Gen 4:5 angry (H2734) stands three words after regard: the Lord's lack of regard for Cain's offering is followed at once by Cain's anger.
observations.grounds: So Cain was very angry

observations.text: In 1Sa 1:16 vexation (H3708A) stands nine words after regard, in the reason Hannah gives against being counted worthless: she has spoken out of anxiety and vexation.
observations.grounds: out of my great anxiety and vexation

observations.text: In Jos 7:21 beautiful (H2896A) describes the cloak Achan saw, nine words before the weighing of the gold bar: both are in his list of what he saw and coveted.
observations.grounds: a beautiful cloak from Shinar

observations.text: In Rom 4:19 and Heb 11:11 faith (G4102G) stands before the considering, as its frame: not weakening in faith when he considered his body, by faith Sarah counted the promiser faithful. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through see and respect; the verses pair the considering with faith.
observations.grounds: since she considered him faithful who had promised

observations.text: In Judg 15:3 harm (H7451C, with H0589 and H5973A at the same place) stands three words after in regard to: Samson declares himself innocent toward the Philistines in the harm he will do.
observations.grounds: when I do them harm

observations.text: In Ecc 2:11 gained (H3504) stands thirteen words after considered, at the end of what the considering found: nothing to be gained under the sun.
observations.grounds: all was vanity and a striving after wind

observations.text: In 1Pe 5:12 grace (G5485) stands nine words after regard, in what the letter declares: the true grace of God; the regard is of Silvanus as faithful.
observations.grounds: this is the true grace of God

observations.text: In Psa 28:5 build (H1129) stands seven words after regard, in the consequence of not regarding the Lord's works: he will tear them down and not build them up.
observations.grounds: build them up no more

observations.text: In Mar 10:42 called (G4341) stands six words before considered: Jesus calls the disciples to him, then speaks of those considered rulers.
observations.grounds: Jesus called them to him

observations.text: In Heb 11:26 reproach (G3680) stands directly after considered as what is counted: the reproach of Christ counted greater wealth than Egypt's treasures.
observations.grounds: He considered the reproach of Christ

observations.text: In Ezr 8:29 chief (H8269) stands two words after weigh: the weighing is to be done before the chief priests.
observations.grounds: weigh them before the chief priests

observations.text: In 1Ki 10:21 and 2Ch 9:20 pure (H5462) describes the gold five words before considered: all was of pure gold, and silver was counted as nothing.
observations.grounds: were of pure gold

observations.text: In Lev 19:23 forbidden (H6190H, H6189) stands two and six words after regard as what the fruit is to be counted: forbidden for three years.
observations.grounds: regard its fruit as forbidden

observations.text: In Neh 13:13 duty (H5921A) stands two words after considered: the treasurers were counted reliable, and their duty follows, to distribute to their brothers. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through respect; the verse pairs counting with duty.
observations.grounds: they were considered reliable

observations.text: In Jos 7:21 hidden (H2934) stands six words after the weighing of the gold bar, at the end of Achan's account: what he weighed in his telling he also hid.
observations.grounds: they are hidden in the earth

observations.text: In Col 2:16 judgment on (G2919) stands eight words before with regard to: no one is to judge them in the matters the link names.
observations.grounds: let no one pass judgment on you

observations.text: In Psa 119:117 continually (H8548) stands two words after regard and qualifies it: the speaker asks to have regard for the statutes without end.
observations.grounds: have regard for your statutes continually

observations.text: In Isa 53:8 transgression (H6588) stands eight words after considered, in what the generation did not consider: the one cut off was stricken for the transgression of the people.
observations.grounds: for the transgression of my people

observations.text: In Deu 9:27 wickedness (H7562, with H2088 and H0413 at the same place) stands three words after regard as what God is asked not to regard: the stubbornness, wickedness and sin of the people.
observations.grounds: Do not regard the stubbornness of this people

observations.text: In Pro 12:10 cruel (H0394) stands five words after regard, on the other side of the contrast: the righteous regard the life of their beast, the mercy of the wicked is cruel.
observations.grounds: the mercy of the wicked is cruel

observations.text: In Exo 5:9 lying (H8267) stands directly after regard as its object: the men are to pay no regard to lying words.
observations.grounds: pay no regard to lying words

observations.text: In 2Ch 5:11 consecrated (H6942G) stands two words before regard: every priest present was set apart, and the regard that is set aside is for the divisions of their service.
observations.grounds: had consecrated themselves, without regard

observations.text: In Eze 18:28 committed (H6213H) stands six words after considered, in what the man considered: the transgressions he had committed, from which he turned away.
observations.grounds: transgressions that he had committed

observations.text: In Isa 13:17 delight (H2654A) stands three words after regard, in the parallel line: no regard for silver, no delight in gold.
observations.grounds: do not delight in gold

observations.text: In Lam 4:16 favor (H2603A) stands seven words after regard, in the parallel lines: the Lord regards them no more, and no favor is shown to the elders.
observations.grounds: no favor to the elders

observations.text: In Act 28:22 desire (G0515) stands seven words before with regard to: the leaders desire to hear Paul's views, and the link names the sect spoken against.
observations.grounds: we desire to hear from you

observations.text: In Job 2:3 destroy (H1104) stands eighteen words after considered, at the end of the Lord's words: Satan incited him to destroy Job without reason.
observations.grounds: to destroy him without reason

observations.text: In Psa 74:20 violence (H2555) stands seven words after regard, in the reason the covenant is to be regarded: the dark places are full of violence.
observations.grounds: full of the habitations of violence

observations.text: In Eze 18:28 die (H4191) closes the verse, ten words after considered: the one who considered and turned away shall not die.
observations.grounds: he shall not die

observations.text: In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 evil (H7451B) stands twelve and thirteen words after considered, in the description of the one considered: he turns away from evil.
observations.grounds: turns away from evil
